newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS SHAKEN AHEAD OF ROMA MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS SHAKEN AHEAD OF ROMA MATCH.

text.p: Never in their far from illustrious history have Nocerina caused so much commotion.

In 90 minutes on Wednesday the struggling third division club brought European Cup holders Juventus back to earth, gave Italian soccer a headache and quite possibly brought disappointment to thousands of Bosnians.

They also gave heart to Roma, reeling from two successive losses and turmoil following the departure of Argentine defender Roberto Trotta, before their serie A home match against Juventus at the Olympic Stadium on Saturday.

What had looked like a match between the rampant league leaders and a downcast and doubt-ridden Roma now looks much more like a clash between two clubs still searching for the right mixture to power their ambitions.
Nocerina, who have beaten first division Piacenza and Perugia in the Italian Cup so far this season, drew 0-0 with Juventus in a third round tie in southern Italy.
Above all, they proved once again that even mighty Juventus can get it as wrong as the rest of them.
Roma's Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi watched Juve -- admittedly minus many first choices but still with Italy's Alessandro del Piero -- labour against the Serie C club.
"He (Bianchi) will have seen for himself that this was not the real Juventus," said Juventus coach Marcello Lippi after the poor southerners doggedly kept a clean sheet.
"We decided to rest several first team players...and Boksic would not have come on had (Alessio) Tacchinardi not been hurt."

Croat Alen Boksic, scorer of two Champions' League goals this season, came on in the 74th minute but was unable to make any more of an impact than a rusty Del Piero who was returning to the team after 25 days out due to injury.

Juventus should win the replay in Turin on November 6, a date that could prove a headache for Italy who are scheduled to play Bosnia in a friendly match in Sarajevo the same day and could find themselves without their Juventus stars.

The result will have added to Roma's resolve while possibly unsettling their opponents who had entered the week on a high, top of the league after beating Inter 2-0 and widely acclaimed as back to their best.
Juventus are on 13 points after six league games while Roma have 10 and need to win to restore some calm and composure.

Roma are certainly capable of winning -- they beat champions Milan 3-0 earlier in the month -- but they must first find a way to recoup the confidence lost after being beaten 3-0 in a UEFA Cup second round first leg tie by Karlsruhe in Germany.
The second leg is at home next week and weekend defeat by Juventus followed by a departure from the UEFA competition would spell big trouble for Bianchi.

The Argentine tried to tackle the problem by sending his troubled protege Roberto Trotta, a player he brought from Argentine club Velez Sarsfeld, back home for a rest in a bid to beat the defender's homesickness and confidence crisis.
"My belief in Trotta is unchanged," he said. "He is the one who does not believe in himself at the moment.
"I cannot be sentimental at times like these. I can only think of the good of the club. I hope that Trotta comes back as the man I recognise."
In the meantime, Roma can expect to welcome their influential Swedish international midfielder Jonas Thern back after an injury layoff as well as Fancesco Statuto.
Thern, who fractured a little toe, still has residual pain and is likely to play with a special protector.
Argentine Abel Balbo looks sure to lead the attack with his striking partner still a matter for conjecture.
